state.product: GrapiX: broadcast graphics (Rust, Windows first). An engine process listens on a control plane (TCP, port 4400, tokens verified per connection) and an asset plane (TCP, control port + 1, publishes and fetches scene packages). Two MCP servers can listen on HTTP. A bind policy (check_bind) exists in the control-plane crate: reserved ports are refused; a token (at least 32 bytes) must be configured to listen off loopback; loopback needs none.
state.audit_findings: A layering audit found: (3) the asset plane binds its own TcpListener and bypasses the bind policy, and it verifies no credential; (4) the engine's --lan flag only declares a locality (it changes timing lead and the media codecs offered), both listeners stay bound to 127.0.0.1 whatever it says, so a LAN engine cannot be reached over a LAN; (10) the same host:port literals (127.0.0.1:4400 and :4401) are repeated in both shells, a launcher script and the worker's port+1 rule, and the MCP server accepts any port with --http while the guard only greps the literal 4100.
state.row: 2.21 (proposed): every listener a product opens passes through the bind policy; a bind off loopback without a token is refused by name for the asset plane and the MCP HTTP server as for the control plane; an engine started with --lan binds its declared interface (and is reached over it in a test) instead of only labelling itself; the repeated literals come from one constants module; the architecture guard refuses a socket bind or a host:port literal outside the allow-listed places.
state.constraints: The asset plane and the MCP HTTP server verify NO credential today (separate rows 2.24 and 2.23 will add that; they need the user's decision). If the policy lets them listen off loopback because a token is configured, they would accept anyone on the network while claiming to be protected. Conformance and tests start engines with --lan on loopback to exercise the LAN transfer path (chunked upload, compressed media) without a second machine. Editor-side crates may not depend on the control-plane client (a guard rule), so shared constants must live in a crate they may use (gx-contracts is the lowest crate). Windows first; no other platform is built or run.

options_offloopback.refuse_until_authenticated: A: the asset plane and the MCP HTTP server go through the same bind function but declare that they cannot authenticate yet; the policy refuses any non-loopback bind for such a plane by name ("this plane verifies no credential: loopback only until it does"). Reserved ports and loopback behave as for the control plane. When rows 2.23/2.24 add verification, the plane declares it can authenticate and the same token rule applies.
options_offloopback.same_rule_with_token: B: the asset plane and the MCP HTTP server use the control plane's rule exactly: a token configured permits a bind off loopback. They do not yet check the token, so this is a policy in name only until 2.23 and 2.24.
options_offloopback.authenticate_now: C: add credential verification to the asset plane and the MCP HTTP server in this row, so the same token rule is true; this enlarges the row into rows 2.23 and 2.24.

options_lan.label_plus_bind_flag: A: --lan stays a declaration of locality (tests keep using it on loopback); a new --bind <ip> chooses the control plane's interface through the bind policy (a token is required off loopback); the asset plane stays on loopback until it can authenticate, and the worker says so at start, so a LAN engine is reachable for control but not yet for publishes.
options_lan.lan_implies_bind: B: --lan means "bind the machine's LAN interface": it requires --bind, and a --lan engine on loopback is no longer possible; tests that exercise the LAN path over loopback need another switch.
options_lan.derive_from_bind: C: remove the --lan flag; locality is derived from the bind address (loopback is co-located, anything else is LAN); the tests that exercise the LAN path on loopback need a test-only override.

options_constants.contracts_endpoints_module: A: a small module in gx-contracts holds the ports and default endpoints (control 4400, asset 4401, the reserved list); every crate that needs one imports it; the control-plane bind module re-exports for compatibility.
options_constants.keep_in_bind_rs: B: leave the ports in the control-plane bind module and make the shells depend on that crate for them.
options_constants.per_crate: C: leave each crate with its own constants and add a test that they agree.

options_guard.allow_list_of_bind_sites: A: the guard fails the build if a socket bind (TcpListener::bind and its tokio form) appears in product code outside an allow-listed set of files, and if a host:port literal for the engine ports appears outside the endpoints module and tests; a new listener must be added to the list on purpose.
options_guard.literal_only: B: the guard only flags host:port literals and reserved ports, and leaves bind calls unwatched.
options_guard.none: C: no new guard rule; rely on review.
